description.value:
Oldenborn.

“You are not an elf. You are the memory of a place that learned to walk again.”

Dream-Flesh. You do not sleep. When you rest, you drift into Yesod—symbolic memory-space—unless you choose otherwise. You are immune to magical sleep, and you can always tell when a dream, illusion, or constructed reality is present.

Old Memory, Old Paths. You reroll the lowest die on checks to interpret ruins, follow ley-lines, identify altered terrain, and sense metaphysical instability. You always know if a place feels remembered, abandoned, or contested (the GM answers vaguely).

Veil-Sight. You perceive the presence of spirits, ghosts, Spark echoes, and noospheric constructs. This grants awareness, not perfect sight.

You Are Remembered. When you first meet a community, the GM chooses (or rolls) whether you are met with reverence, fear, or familiarity. It’s never neutral.

description.value:
Oldenborn Heritage. The branch that stayed in the dirt. Bone of the bedrock, slow blood, slow grudge. The land remembers your name and answers when you call.

“The world remembered old names. You answered.”

Earthbound. You are the place-soul that put down roots and refused to be moved. Folks call you a stout one—dwarf, gnome, hill spirit, depending on the dialect. The truth is older than any of those words.

Traits

  • Creature Type. Humanoid (Fey).

  • Size. Medium.

  • Lineage Lean. Your lineage leans toward BOD (Body)—expressed primarily through Tier powers.

  • Stoneborn. You reroll the lowest die on checks to resist being knocked prone or forcibly moved while you stand on natural ground.

advancement.hint: Gain your Earthbound Tier I lineage power (Stonecall).

description.value:
“Stone remembers pressure. So do you.”

Stonecall (1/Soma Break). When you plant your feet, the world updates its assumptions about where “down” is. Until the start of your next turn, you can’t be forcibly moved, you have resistance to kinetic damage, and you ignore difficult terrain caused by earth, rubble, or broken masonry.

effects.name: Earthbound: Stonecall (Passive Athletics)
effects.description: Represents bracing instinct. The core Stonecall effects are enforced at the table.

description.value:
"Set your feet. The line forms on you."

The Bulwark is the wall — and the wall runs on Surge, like everyone, but yours arrives the hard way: every time you take Integrity damage you bank +1 Surge (max +2/round (+3 with Polarity Mastery, Mountain)). You eat the blow and turn it into the power to anchor, erupt, or hold. At zero Surge you still stand in the way; soak one hit and your turn opens up.

The Fortress (spent via Surge — Bulwark only)

  • Brace Wall (1) — you and adjacent allies gain DR equal to Tier this round.

  • Bulwark Stance (6) — adjacent allies share your defenses until your next turn.

  • Anchor (5) — you and one ally become immune to forced movement and crowd-control until next round.

  • Mass Aegis (8) — allies within Tier squares gain +Tier to every defense this round.

  • Sanctum (9) — immune to one damage type for a round.

  • Mythic Stand (10) — invulnerable until the start of your next turn.

These were always the Bulwark's birthright; they no longer leak into everyone else's menu. The old Frame and Ruin tricks are Surge spends too — Absorb (1), Push (1), Shockwave Footing (2), Catastrophic Entry (3), Siege Works (2) and Ruin to Renewal (3) — and your Path adds three more of its own.

system.source: Bad Eden Bulwark + Shadow Courier v1.0 (RFI-native rules)

description.value:
The world has two ways of saying no to change. You learn one of them today.

On gaining Bulwark Initiation 1 you receive:

  • Skill rank +1 in Athletics (Violence).

  • Skill rank +1 in Melee and Plating.

  • +30 Violence marks to your Domain's cap, and 20 marks of free siege works folded into the buffer every time your Domain opens or joins a Siege.

  • You bank Surge by eating the blow: +1 Surge each time you take Integrity damage (max +2 a round). Spend it from the ◆ Surge menu.

Your Path's L1 feature shapes how you bank it.

description.value:
"You belong here now. Argue with the mountain."

Doctrine: Durability, refusal, rootedness — immovable, load-bearing, patient.

The Mountain makes the scene bounce off you. Your Surge spends are the geometry of refusal: roots that share their footing, a flat "no" to the next thing done to you or yours, and a bastion the whole line forms behind.

Path (spent via Surge)

  • Root (1) — you and adjacent allies gain DR equal to Tier and cannot be forcibly moved.
  • Deny (2) — you or an ally becomes immune to forced-movement/CC and gains DR this round.
  • Bastion (5) — allies within Tier squares gain DR equal to Tier; you cannot be moved.

Nothing that stands can be moved. Your inevitability is the kind that absorbs.

Mode: Immovable Object / drift: Away.

You bank Surge by absorbing damage rather than by breaking things: each Integrity hit you take banks +1 Surge (max +2 a round, +3 once Polarity Mastery arrives).

Anchor Point

The world pushes. You remain.

Rules

You reroll the lowest die on checks or saves made to resist being pushed, pulled, knocked prone, Shaken, or charmed.

⚙ Reroll-lowest on checks and defense checks; the push / pull / prone / Shaken / charm gate is read by the GM.

description.value:
You decide which side of you is the wall.

Reaction. When a creature within 1 square of you attempts to move past you (toward a square that would put you between it and where it came from), you may spend 1 Surge as a reaction. Its movement simply ends in its current square — no attack roll, no defense check. It has not yet spent the movement and may retreat or take a different path next turn.

Limit: once per target per encounter. Use the ▶ button with the creature targeted.

Bound and Bargained

A sealed pact holds itself; you need only keep the terms.

Rules

While your Sealed Pact stance is active, the bindings carry part of your will for you: your Clarity maximum rises by 1.

description.value:
Signature move. Once a scene, you choose which kind of inevitability you are.

Anchor or Advance — 1/scene (recovers on Soma Break). As part of any action on your turn, declare a stance. The chosen stance lasts until the end of your next turn:

  • Anchor. You cannot be moved against your will by any effect short of a Heroic-DC (22) push from a creature of your size or larger. Forced movement, knockback, teleportation targeting you, banishment, and dimensional swap effects all fail.

  • Advance. You cannot be prevented from reaching a destination you declare on the same action. Difficult terrain, conditions that halve speed, reaction strikes, and zone-of-control effects do not stop your movement toward that point. You may still take damage along the way.

Doctrine features at L5+ extend or modify which stance you favor.

Bladed Tempo

Your weapons are punctuation.

Rules

When you hit with a melee weapon attack, you may immediately draw or stow a weapon, or shift 1 square without provoking reaction strikes.

✍ Table rule.

description.value:
Time itself counts as ground you have claimed.

You cannot be moved from a space you have occupied for at least one full round, except by a single damage instance equal to or greater than your current Integrity value. This denial covers, but is not limited to:

  • Forced movement of any kind (push, pull, slide, throw)

  • Teleportation effects targeting you

  • Banishment, dimensional swap, and plane-shift effects

  • Knockback from area-of-effect damage

  • Grapple and drag attempts

You may end the Hold voluntarily as a free action on your turn. After moving voluntarily, you must occupy a new space for one full round before the Hold protects you again.

system.requirements: Path of the Mountain, Bulwark Initiation 9
